nodes.description:
Identify usages for either a semantic symbol, or the symbol(s) implied
by a source range.
Ordering and uniqueness guarantees:
1. The usages returned will already be de-duplicated.
2. Results are first grouped by provenance in the order precise, syntactic, then search-based.
3. Results for a single repository are contiguous.
4. Results for a single file are contiguous.
Related: See `codeGraphData` on GitBlob.

EXPERIMENTAL: This API may make backwards-incompatible changes in the future.
nodes.name: usagesForSymbol

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Lists synchronized code-host change requests, newest first
by creation time on the code host. Only signed-in users can list change
requests, and only while the bacon feature flag is enabled. The viewer only
sees change requests of repositories they can access on Sourcegraph; site
administrators also see those of repositories that aren't on Sourcegraph.
nodes.name: changeRequests

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Looks up a synchronized code-host change request by ID. Returns
null if it does not exist or the viewer can't access its repository (see
changeRequests). Only signed-in users can look up change requests, and only
while the bacon feature flag is enabled.
nodes.name: changeRequest

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Code-host capabilities for a changeset and the viewer's linked
account. Requires the same access as changeRequest. Capabilities are scoped
to this changeset, not global properties of the code host.
nodes.name: codeHostCapabilities

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Looks up a review report by ID. Any viewer who can look up
change requests and access the report's repository can open a report by ID,
not only its creator. Returns null if it does not exist or the repository
is not available to the viewer.
nodes.name: changeRequestReport

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: The distinct prompts the viewer requested review reports
with, for any change request, most recently used first. Considers the
viewer's 100 newest reports. Unlike reports, prompts are returned even if a
report's repository is no longer available to the viewer, because the
viewer wrote them.
nodes.name: viewerRecentReportPrompts

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Looks up a synchronized code-host change request by repository
and number. Returns null if it does not exist or the viewer can't access its
repository (see changeRequests). Only signed-in users can look up change
requests, and only while the bacon feature flag is enabled.
nodes.name: changeRequestByRepository

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Searches the labels of change requests, ordered by exact
matches, then names that start with the text, then the rest by name.
Labels whose names differ only in case are one label. The viewer only sees
labels of repositories they can access on Sourcegraph (see changeRequests);
each label has the spelling and color of the accessible repository where it
was seen most recently. Labels that change requests no longer have can
still appear for up to a day. Only signed-in users can search labels, and
only while the bacon feature flag is enabled. Currently supports GitHub.
nodes.name: changeRequestLabels

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Searches the code-host teams that change requests requested a
review from, ordered by organization and slug. The viewer only sees the teams
of organizations with a change request visible to them (see
changeRequests), including teams without current review requests. Only
signed-in users can search teams, and only while the bacon feature flag is
enabled.
nodes.name: changeRequestTeams

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Looks up a code-host team that change requests requested a
review from, by its organization and slug, ignoring case. Returns null if
there is no such team or the viewer can't see it (see changeRequestTeams).
Names are refreshed when a change request that requests the team is
synchronized, so if a renamed team's previous name was taken by another
team, returns the most recently added one. Only signed-in users can look up
teams, and only while the bacon feature flag is enabled.
nodes.name: changeRequestTeam

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: The Semgrep connection that provides security scan results
for changesets, or null if Semgrep is not connected. Requires the
INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#READ permission and the bacon feature flag.
nodes.name: reviewSemgrepConnection

nodes.description:

nodes.description:
Checks the MCP server at url before a connector is created: its name,
whether it requires authentication, and whether connectors can use OAuth
with it, like createConnector does.

Checks for personal connectors (personal: true) behave like personal
connectors: they require the CONNECTORS#WRITE_USER permission, and they can
only reach servers on public addresses, so they can't check servers on
private networks. Other checks require the INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#WRITE
permission.
nodes.name: discoverConnector

secret does not yet exist in the target namespace, it is created with the
supplied credential as its single entry.
Exactly one of (`username` + `password`) or `auth` must be supplied:
  - When `username` and `password` are supplied, the server encodes
    `base64(username:password)` and stores that as the credential.
  - When `auth` is supplied, it must already be a `base64(username:password)`
    string (e.g. taken from `docker login`'s `~/.docker/config.json`).
Only BATCHES scope is currently supported.

User ID or an Org ID. Non-admins may only target their own user namespace
or an org they belong to; site admins may target any namespace. When

is targeted; this is restricted to site admins.

mutation will be revoked for the role.
nodes.name: mutation.setRoles

nodes.description: Creates the entitlement. Site-admin only.
nodes.name: mutation.createEntitlement

nodes.description: Updates the entitlement. Site-admin only.
nodes.name: mutation.updateEntitlement

nodes.description: Deletes the entitlement. Site-admin only.
nodes.name: mutation.deleteEntitlement

nodes.description: Grants the entitlement to the users. Site-admin only.
nodes.name: mutation.createEntitlementGrants

nodes.description: Deletes the entitlement grants. Site-admin only.
nodes.name: mutation.deleteEntitlementGrants

nodes.description: Resets entitlement usage for a user. Site-admin only.
nodes.name: mutation.resetEntitlementUsage

nodes.description:
Telemetry mutations for "Event Logging Everywhere", aka a version 2 of
existing event-logging/event-recording APIs.
nodes.name: mutation.telemetry

nodes.description: Create a prompt.
nodes.name: mutation.createPrompt

nodes.description: Update a prompt.
nodes.name: mutation.updatePrompt

nodes.description: Delete a prompt.
nodes.name: mutation.deletePrompt

nodes.description:
Transfer ownership of a prompt to a new owner (a namespace, either a user or organization).

Only users who can administer the prompt may transfer it.
nodes.name: mutation.transferPromptOwnership

nodes.description:
Change the visibility state of a prompt.

Only users who can administer the prompt may change its visibility state.
nodes.name: mutation.changePromptVisibility

nodes.description: Create a prompt tag.
nodes.name: mutation.createPromptTag

nodes.description: Update a prompt tag.
nodes.name: mutation.updatePromptTag

nodes.description: Delete a prompt tag.
nodes.name: mutation.deletePromptTag

nodes.description:
Create a new IdP client. The secret will be returned and can never be accessed
again.

Requires IDP_CLIENTS#WRITE permission.
nodes.name: mutation.createIDPClient

nodes.description:
Update an existing IdP client.

Requires IDP_CLIENTS#WRITE permission.
nodes.name: mutation.updateIDPClient

nodes.description:
Delete an existing IdP client. Caution: all access tokens issued by this client
are no longer usable.

Requires IDP_CLIENTS#WRITE permission.
nodes.name: mutation.deleteIDPClient

nodes.description:
Make a determination for device authorization. Identified by the user code from
the authorization flow.
nodes.name: mutation.resolveDeviceAuthorization

nodes.description:
Revoke the UserConsentedIDPClient consent.
This will invalidate all access tokens and refresh tokens issued to this client
for the current user, and force a consent prompt for the next authorization flow.

Can only be called by the user who owns the consent, or a site-admin.
nodes.name: mutation.revokeIDPClientConsent

nodes.description:
Create a new M2M (Machine-to-Machine) credential for a service account.
This creates an IdP client that can use client credentials flow to obtain
access tokens with the service account as the subject.

Requires IDP_CLIENTS#WRITE_IMPERSONATION permission.
nodes.name: mutation.createM2MCredential

nodes.description:
Delete an M2M credential for a service account.
This will delete the associated IdP client and invalidate all access tokens.

Requires IDP_CLIENTS#WRITE_IMPERSONATION permission.
nodes.name: mutation.deleteM2MCredential

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Updates a changeset's description as the viewer's linked
code-host account. Checks the live description against expectedBody before
writing. The code host enforces permissions. Conflict detection is best
effort: a concurrent edit on the host between the check and write can be overwritten.
nodes.name: mutation.updateChangeRequestDescription

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Updates a changeset's title as the viewer's linked code-host
account. Removes surrounding whitespace, and rejects empty and multi-line
titles. Checks the live title against expectedTitle before writing. The
code host enforces permissions. Conflict detection is best effort: a
concurrent edit on the host between the check and write can be overwritten.
nodes.name: mutation.updateChangeRequestTitle

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Merges one changeset as the viewer's linked code-host account.
Rechecks readiness and atomically requires the displayed head to match.
Requires the same access as changeRequest. Does not bypass code-host rules.
nodes.name: mutation.mergeChangeRequest

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Marks one draft changeset ready for review as the viewer's
linked code-host account. Succeeds without a change if it is already ready
for review. Requires the same access as changeRequest; the code host
enforces permissions. Currently supports GitHub.
nodes.name: mutation.markChangeRequestReadyForReview

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Closes one open changeset without merging it, as the viewer's
linked code-host account. Succeeds without a change if it is already
closed. Requires the same access as changeRequest; the code host enforces
permissions. Currently supports GitHub.
nodes.name: mutation.closeChangeRequest

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Reopens one closed changeset as the viewer's linked code-host
account. Succeeds without a change if it is already open. Requires the same
access as changeRequest; the code host enforces permissions. Currently
supports GitHub.
nodes.name: mutation.reopenChangeRequest

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Requests reviews of one open changeset as the viewer's
linked code-host account, in addition to the reviewers already requested.
Requires the same access as changeRequest; the code host enforces
permissions. Currently supports GitHub.
nodes.name: mutation.requestChangeRequestReviews

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Removes review requests of one open changeset as the viewer's
linked code-host account. Reviewers that the changeset doesn't request are
ignored. Requires the same access as changeRequest; the code host enforces
permissions. Currently supports GitHub.
nodes.name: mutation.removeChangeRequestReviewRequests

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Moves one file to a review category for all viewers. Only
the author may edit; the synchronized base and head must still match.
nodes.name: mutation.moveChangeRequestFile

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Reports whether the viewer is looking at, reviewing, and
typing a chat message about a change request in one browser session, and
returns the users looking at it or who looked at it in the last 4 hours:
the viewer first, then those looking at it, and the rest most recent first.
Clients report active about every 15 seconds while the page is visible, or
every 5 seconds while others are looking at it, and inactive when it is
hidden or closed. A session stops counting 45 seconds after its last active
report.
nodes.name: mutation.reportChangeRequestPresence

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Requests a review report of the change request's current
synchronized head, shaped by the viewer's prompt. Generation is
asynchronous: the report starts QUEUED, and its document fills in as the
agent works. Poll changeRequestReport for progress.
nodes.name: mutation.createChangeRequestReport

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Sends a message to the change request's chat as the viewer.
The message is stored only in Sourcegraph, not posted to the code host.
nodes.name: mutation.sendChangeRequestChatMessage

nodes.description: EXPERIMENTAL: Deletes one of the viewer's own chat messages.
nodes.name: mutation.deleteChangeRequestChatMessage

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Replaces the text of one of the viewer's own chat messages,
which is possible for 30 minutes after sending it. Mentions added by
editing don't notify anyone.
nodes.name: mutation.editChangeRequestChatMessage

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Submits a review for a code-host change request. The initial
implementation supports GitHub pull requests only.
nodes.name: mutation.submitChangeRequestReview

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Posts a general conversation comment as the viewer, independently
of any pending review. Initially supports GitHub pull requests only.
nodes.name: mutation.addChangeRequestComment

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Starts a thread of inline comments on a change request's
diff as the viewer's linked code-host account. The comment is posted
immediately. Currently supports GitHub.
nodes.name: mutation.addChangeRequestReviewThread

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Replies to a thread of inline comments as the viewer's linked
code-host account. Currently supports GitHub.
nodes.name: mutation.replyToChangeRequestReviewThread

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Deletes a comment of a change request review thread as the
viewer's linked code-host account, if the code host allows it. Currently
supports GitHub.
nodes.name: mutation.deleteChangeRequestReviewComment

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Connects Semgrep to show security scan results on
changesets, replacing any existing connection. Requires the
INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#WRITE permission and the bacon feature flag.
nodes.name: mutation.connectReviewSemgrep

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Disconnects Semgrep. Sourcegraph stops requesting scan
results; results already shown on changesets remain. Requires the
INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#WRITE permission and the bacon feature flag.
nodes.name: mutation.disconnectReviewSemgrep

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Creates a rule that turns references in changeset
descriptions into links. Requires the INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#WRITE
permission and the bacon feature flag.
nodes.name: mutation.createReviewDescriptionLinkRule

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Deletes a description link rule. Requires the
INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#WRITE permission and the bacon feature flag.
nodes.name: mutation.deleteReviewDescriptionLinkRule

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Sends a direct message with a link to link the viewer's Slack
account. The Sourcegraph Slack app sends it to the account in a connected
Slack workspace whose email address is a verified email address of the
viewer. Opening the link signed in as the viewer and passing its token to
linkReviewSlackAccount links the account. The link expires after 15
minutes. Requires a signed-in user and the bacon feature flag.
nodes.name: mutation.requestReviewSlackAccountLink

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Links the Slack account that received the token from
requestReviewSlackAccountLink to the viewer, replacing the viewer's
previously linked account. Only the viewer who requested the token can use
it. The Sourcegraph Slack app then sends the account a direct message when
a changeset requests a review from the viewer's linked code-host account.
Requires a signed-in user and the bacon feature flag.
nodes.name: mutation.linkReviewSlackAccount

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Unlinks the viewer's Slack account, if they linked one.
Requires a signed-in user and the bacon feature flag.
nodes.name: mutation.unlinkReviewSlackAccount

nodes.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Mutations on compendia. Require the COMPENDIA#WRITE
permission.
nodes.name: mutation.compendia

nodes.description:
Creates a connector after checking that Sourcegraph can talk to it. For
connectors with shared credentials, this lists the server's tools. For
OAuth connectors, this discovers the authorization server and registers
Sourcegraph as an OAuth client.

Personal connectors require the CONNECTORS#WRITE_USER permission. Other
connectors require the INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#WRITE permission.
nodes.name: mutation.createConnector

nodes.description:
Updates a connector and checks connectivity like createConnector. Users
have to connect again if the server or OAuth client changes, for example
because the instance's external URL changed.

Requires the INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#WRITE permission, or owning the
personal connector and the CONNECTORS#WRITE_USER permission, like all
mutations that manage a connector.
nodes.name: mutation.updateConnector

nodes.description: Deletes a connector and all user authorizations for it.
nodes.name: mutation.deleteConnector

nodes.description:
Enables or disables tools of a connector. Tools are enabled by default,
except tools that may delete or overwrite data, which includes tools
without hints about their effects.
nodes.name: mutation.setConnectorToolsEnabled

nodes.description:
Connects to a connector, lists its tools again, and stores them, so it also
checks that Sourcegraph can reach the server and authenticate. Connectors
with per-user authorization use the current user's authorization.
nodes.name: mutation.refreshConnectorTools

nodes.description:
Removes the current user's authorization for a connector with per-user
authorization.
nodes.name: mutation.disconnectConnector

nodes.description:
Stores the current user's API token for a connector with per-user tokens,
after checking that the server accepts it. For USER_BASIC, token is
base64(username:password), without the Basic prefix; the password can be
an API token.
nodes.name: mutation.setConnectorUserToken

nodes.description:
Turns a connector off or on for one kind of the current user's agents.
Connectors are on by default.
nodes.name: mutation.setConnectorDisabled

specification.text:
"""
A provider serving models from the customer's AWS account through Amazon
Bedrock's runtime endpoint: Claude models
(https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-messages-api.html),
and OpenAI GPT models
(https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-responses-api.html).
Models must be explicitly selected with the Bedrock model or inference profile
ID they are served under; automatic coverage is not supported.
"""
type AWSBedrockInferenceProvider implements Node & InferenceProvider {
  """The provider's unique identifier."""
  id: ID!

  """The provider's display name."""
  name: String!

  """The AWS region serving the models, such as us-east-1."""
  region: String!

  """
  The bedrock-runtime endpoint derived from region, such as
  https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com.
  """
  endpoint: String!

  """The provider's authentication configuration."""
  authentication: InferenceProviderAuthentication!

  """Model routes configured explicitly on this provider."""
  explicitModelRoutes: [InferenceProviderExplicitModelRoute!]!

  """
  Always false; Amazon Bedrock provider models require explicit selection.
  """
  automaticCoverage: Boolean!

  """Canonical model references excluded from automatic coverage."""
  excludedModelRefs: [String!]!
}

"""Access request"""
type AccessRequest implements Node {
  """The unique identifier of the secret."""
  id: ID!

  """Name of a person requested access"""
  name: String!

  """Email of a person requested access"""
  email: String!

  """The date and time when request access was created"""
  createdAt: DateTime!

  """Additional information submitted by person requested access"""
  additionalInfo: String

  """Access request status"""
  status: AccessRequestStatus!
}

"""A list of access requests"""
type AccessRequestConnection {
  """Total count of access requests"""
  totalCount: Int!

  """A list of access requests"""
  nodes: [AccessRequest!]!

  """Pagination information."""
  pageInfo: BidirectionalPageInfo!
}

"""Access request status enum"""
enum AccessRequestStatus {
  """Access request is submitted and waiting for actions"""
  PENDING

  """Access request was approved"""
  APPROVED

  """Access request was rejected"""
  REJECTED

  """Access request was canceled"""
  CANCELED
}

"""Input for configuring access restrictions in site configuration."""
input AccessRestrictionsConfigurationInput {
  """Whether repository permissions are enforced for site admins."""
  enforceForSiteAdmins: Boolean!

  """Whether IP allowlist is enabled."""
  ipAllowlistEnabled: Boolean!

  """Allowed user IP addresses (CIDR notation supported)."""
  userIpAddress: [String!]!

  """Allowed client IP addresses (e.g., load balancer ranges)."""
  clientIpAddress: [String!]!

  """Trusted client IP addresses that bypass user IP checks."""
  trustedClientIpAddress: [String!]!

  """Request headers to check for user IP address."""
  userIpRequestHeaders: [String!]!

  """Custom error message shown when access is denied."""
  errorMessageTemplate: String!
}

"""
An access token that grants to the holder the privileges of the user who created it.
"""
type AccessToken implements Node {
  """The unique ID for the access token."""
  id: ID!

  """
  The user whose privileges the access token grants.
  Returns null if the subject user has been deleted.
  """
  subject: User

  """
  The scopes that define the allowed set of operations that can be performed using this access token.
  """
  scopes: [String!]!

  """A user-supplied descriptive note for the access token."""
  note: String!

  """
  The user who created the access token. This is either the subject user (if the access token
  was created by the same user) or a site admin (who can create access tokens for any user).
  Returns null if the creator user has been deleted.
  """
  creator: User

  """The date when the access token was created."""
  createdAt: DateTime!

  """
  The date when the access token was last used to authenticate a request.
  """
  lastUsedAt: DateTime

  """If non-null, the token may no longer be used after this date."""
  expiresAt: DateTime

  """
  The last 5 characters of the token, useful for identifying which token is configured.
  Only available for tokens created starting with Sourcegraph 6.13.
  """
  tokenLastChars: String

  """
  The date when the access token was deleted. Deleted tokens can no longer be used, but their
  records are retained. Null if the token has not been deleted.
  """
  deletedAt: DateTime
}

"""A list of access tokens."""
type AccessTokenConnection {
  """A list of access tokens."""
  nodes: [AccessToken!]!

  """
  The total count of access tokens in the connection. This total count may be larger than the number of nodes
  in this object when the result is paginated.
  """
  totalCount: Int!

  """Pagination information."""
  pageInfo: PageInfo!
}

"""Policy for access token creation."""
enum AccessTokensAllowPolicy {
  """All users can create access tokens."""
  ALL_USERS_CREATE

  """
  Only site admins can create access tokens (existing tokens still work until revoked).
  """
  SITE_ADMIN_CREATE

  """Access tokens are disabled entirely."""
  NONE
}

"""Access token configuration input."""
input AccessTokensInput {
  """Allow or restrict the use of access tokens."""
  allow: AccessTokensAllowPolicy!

  """Whether to allow tokens without expiration."""
  allowNoExpiration: Boolean!
}

"""
Input for posting a general comment, without a file or revision anchor.
"""
input AddChangeRequestCommentInput {
  """The change request to comment on."""
  changeRequest: ID!

  """The comment as code-host markup."""
  body: String!
}

"""Input for starting a change request review thread."""
input AddChangeRequestReviewThreadInput {
  """The change request to comment on."""
  changeRequest: ID!

  """
  The head commit of the diff the lines refer to. It must be the change
  request's current head on the code host.
  """
  expectedHeadOID: GitObjectID!

  """The path of the commented file in the diff."""
  path: String!

  """The side containing the first line."""
  startSide: DiffAnchorSide!

  """The first line, inclusive, in the file on startSide."""
  startLine: Int!

  """The side containing the last line."""
  endSide: DiffAnchorSide!

  """The last line, inclusive, in the file on endSide."""
  endLine: Int!

  """The comment as code-host markup."""
  body: String!
}

"""A note for the generator of a compendium."""
input AddCompendiumNoteInput {
  """The compendium."""
  compendium: ID!

  """The note, in plain text."""
  body: String!

  """
  A data URL (image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif or image/webp, at most
  4 MB) such as a photo of a hand-drawn diagram; it informs the directions
  but is never shown to readers.
  """
  image: String
}

"""A new external service."""
input AddExternalServiceInput {
  """The kind of the external service."""
  kind: ExternalServiceKind!

  """The display name of the external service."""
  displayName: String!

  """The JSON configuration of the external service."""
  config: String!

  """
  The namespace this external service belongs to.
  This can be used both for a user and an organization.
  """
  namespace: ID
}

"""Input object for adding insight view to dashboard."""
input AddInsightViewToDashboardInput {
  """ID of the insight view to attach to the dashboard"""
  insightViewId: ID!

  """ID of the dashboard."""
  dashboardId: ID!
}

"""Information regarding the availablity of a SearchAggregationMode"""
type AggregationGroup {
  """
  A label associated with the Aggregation for example a Repo name or Author name
  """
  label: String!

  """The number of hits for this search"""
  count: Int!

  """
  A modified search query that would filter the orginal query to just the selected group
  """
  query: String
}

"""Information regarding the availablity of a SearchAggregationMode"""
type AggregationModeAvailability {
  """The SearchAggregationMode"""
  mode: SearchAggregationMode!

  """Boolean indicating if the mode is available"""
  available: Boolean!

  """If the mode is unavailable the reason why"""
  reasonUnavailable: String
}

"""An alert message shown to the viewer."""
type Alert {
  """The type of this alert."""
  type: AlertType!

  """The message body of this alert. Markdown is supported."""
  message: String!

  """
  If set, this alert is dismissible. After being dismissed, no other alerts with the same
  isDismissibleWithKey value will be shown. If null, this alert is not dismissible.
  """
  isDismissibleWithKey: String

  """
  The intended audience for this alert. Defaults to SITEADMIN if not specified.
  """
  audience: AlertAudience!
}

"""The intended audience for an alert."""
enum AlertAudience {
  """The alert should be shown to all users."""
  EVERYONE

  """The alert should only be shown to site administrators."""
  SITEADMIN
}

"""The possible types of alerts (Alert.type values)."""
enum AlertType {
  INFO
  WARNING
  ERROR
}

"""A provider implementing an Anthropic-compatible API."""
type AnthropicCompatibleInferenceProvider implements Node & InferenceProvider {
  """The provider's unique identifier."""
  id: ID!

  """The provider's display name."""
  name: String!

  """
  The provider's API base URL, following the vendor SDK convention:
  the origin for Anthropic APIs (https://api.anthropic.com) and the
  versioned base for OpenAI APIs (https://api.openai.com/v1). Request paths
  such as /v1/messages or /chat/completions are appended per protocol.
  """
  endpoint: String!

  """The provider's authentication configuration."""
  authentication: InferenceProviderAuthentication!

  """Model routes configured explicitly on this provider."""
  explicitModelRoutes: [InferenceProviderExplicitModelRoute!]!

  """
  Whether this provider automatically covers compatible models from its publisher.
  """
  automaticCoverage: Boolean!

  """Canonical model references excluded from automatic coverage."""
  excludedModelRefs: [String!]!
}

"""A provider using Anthropic's hosted API."""
type AnthropicInferenceProvider implements Node & InferenceProvider {
  """The provider's unique identifier."""
  id: ID!

  """The provider's display name."""
  name: String!

  """
  The provider's API base URL, following the vendor SDK convention:
  the origin for Anthropic APIs (https://api.anthropic.com) and the
  versioned base for OpenAI APIs (https://api.openai.com/v1). Request paths
  such as /v1/messages or /chat/completions are appended per protocol.
  """
  endpoint: String!

  """The provider's authentication configuration."""
  authentication: InferenceProviderAuthentication!

  """Model routes configured explicitly on this provider."""
  explicitModelRoutes: [InferenceProviderExplicitModelRoute!]!

  """
  Whether this provider automatically covers compatible models from its publisher.
  """
  automaticCoverage: Boolean!

  """Canonical model references excluded from automatic coverage."""
  excludedModelRefs: [String!]!
}

"""A Deep Search conversation to bind to a part of a compendium."""
input AttachCompendiumThreadInput {
  """The compendium."""
  compendium: ID!

  """The Deep Search conversation's ID."""
  conversationID: ID!

  """The part of the compendium the conversation was asked about."""
  anchorKind: CompendiumThreadAnchorKind!

  """The chapter or diagram node id; omitted for the compendium as a whole."""
  anchorID: String
}

"""
AttributionSnippetThreshold describes whether search snippet was considered
large enough to run the search, and what are the thresholds.
"""
type AttributionSnippetThreshold {
  """Whether or not search for the snippet parameter was run."""
  searchPerformed: Boolean!

  """
  Lower bound of lines that Cody considers for attribution search (if any).
  """
  linesLowerBound: Int!
}

"""Represents a state transition of a single column."""
type AuditLogColumnChange {
  """The column that is changing."""
  column: String!

  """The previous value of the column."""
  old: String

  """The new value of the column"""
  new: String
}

"""Denotes the type of operation of a given log entry."""
enum AuditLogOperation {
  """Denotes this log entry represents an INSERT query."""
  CREATE

  """Denotes this log entry represents an UPDATE query."""
  MODIFY
}

"""
A provider of user authentication, such as an external single-sign-on service (e.g., using OpenID Connect or
SAML). The provider information in this type is visible to all viewers and does not contain any secret values.
"""
type AuthProvider {
  """The type of the auth provider."""
  serviceType: String!

  """
  A stable identifier for this provider's configuration, derived deterministically
  from the provider's config without requiring network I/O. Used together with
  serviceType to uniquely identify a provider for mutations.
  """
  configID: String!

  """An identifier for the service that the auth provider represents."""
  serviceID: String!

  """
  An identifier for the client of the service that the auth provider represents.
  """
  clientID: String!

  """The human-readable name of the provider."""
  displayName: String!

  """
  Whether this auth provider is the builtin username-password auth provider.
  """
  isBuiltin: Boolean!

  """
  A URL that, when visited, initiates the authentication process for this auth provider.
  """
  authenticationURL: String

  """
  Whether this auth provider is currently enabled for sign-in (not hidden and not marked as noSignIn).
  """
  isSignInEnabled: Boolean!

  """
  Whether this auth provider can be used for repository permissions syncing.
  This is true for code host auth providers (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud, Bitbucket Server, Gerrit, Azure DevOps).
  """
  isPermissionsProvider: Boolean!

  """
  Whether users must connect an external account for this provider before they
  can continue using Sourcegraph. Only applies to permissions providers whose
  code host enforces repository permissions.
  """
  enforceAccountConnection: Boolean!

  """Whether this auth provider is hidden from the sign-in page."""
  hidden: Boolean!

  """
  Whether this auth provider supports sign-in. Some providers (e.g. Gerrit) are
  permissions-only and cannot be used for sign-in even if configured.
  """
  supportsSignIn: Boolean!

  """
  The display order of this provider on the sign-in page. Providers with lower
  order values appear first. Null means no explicit order is set.
  """
  order: Int
}

"""A list of authentication providers."""
type AuthProviderConnection {
  """A list of authentication providers."""
  nodes: [AuthProvider!]!

  """
  The total count of authentication providers in the connection. This total count may be larger than the number of nodes
  in this object when the result is paginated.
  """
  totalCount: Int!

  """Pagination information."""
  pageInfo: PageInfo!
}

"""Input for identifying an auth provider for reordering."""
input AuthProviderReorderInput {
  """
  The service type of the auth provider (e.g., "github", "gitlab", "saml").
  """
  serviceType: String!

  """The stable configuration identifier of the auth provider."""
  configID: String!
}

"""The result of validating an authentication provider configuration."""
type AuthProviderValidationResult {
  """Whether authentication succeeded."""
  success: Boolean!

  """Error message if authentication failed."""
  errorMessage: String

  """The unique identifier from the IdP (e.g., SAML NameID, OIDC sub)."""
  subject: String

  """The email address extracted from the auth response."""
  email: String

  """The username that would be used/created."""
  username: String

  """The display name from the auth response."""
  displayName: String

  """The groups the user belongs to (if group sync is configured)."""
  groups: [String!]
}

"""An in-progress auth provider wizard configuration."""
type AuthProviderWizardDraft implements Node {
  """The unique ID of this draft."""
  id: ID!

  """The type of wizard."""
  wizardType: AuthWizardType!

  """Optional display name for this draft."""
  displayName: String

comparator fields within a filter are combined. Omitted filters and
comparator fields are unrestricted.
"""

  """The change request's state."""
  state: ChangeRequestStateComparator

  """Whether the change request is a draft."""
  draft: ChangeRequestBooleanComparator

  """
  The author. A Sourcegraph user matches linked code-host accounts or verified
  emails in the stored payload. A code-host account matches its login on that
  code host. Currently supports GitHub, so nin matches all change requests on
  other code hosts.
  """
  author: ChangeRequestParticipantComparator

  """
  The reviewers from whom a review is currently requested. Does not imply a
  state or draft filter.
  
  A Sourcegraph user includes direct and team requests, unless via restricts
  them to one of the two. Direct requests match a linked code-host account or
  verified email in the stored payload. Team requests require a linked GitHub
  account and app-synchronized membership from the last 30 minutes, so none
  still matches team requests whose membership is stale. Membership is
  refreshed periodically using Review GitHub App installations with
  Organization members: read permission.
  
  A code-host account matches only direct requests for its login on that code
  host. A team matches only requests of the team itself, regardless of its
  membership. Currently supports GitHub.
  """
  requestedReviewers: ChangeRequestParticipantCollectionComparator

  """
  The code host's overall review status as of the last synchronization. Does
  not imply a state filter. Currently supports GitHub.
  """
  reviewStatus: ChangeRequestReviewStatusComparator

  """The repository name on the code host, such as owner/name."""
  repository: ChangeRequestStringComparator

  """

  change requests of both archived and active repositories.

  repositoryArchived: ChangeRequestBooleanComparator

  """The code-host base URL. Equality ignores a trailing slash."""
  codeHostURL: ChangeRequestStringComparator

  """When the change request was created on the code host."""
  createdAt: ChangeRequestDateComparator

  """When the change request was last updated on the code host."""
  updatedAt: ChangeRequestDateComparator

  """
  When the change request was merged. Excludes change requests that were not
  merged.
  """
  mergedAt: ChangeRequestDateComparator

  """
  When the change request was closed on the code host. Excludes change
  requests that were not closed. Code hosts such as GitHub also report a close
  time for merged change requests.
  """
  closedAt: ChangeRequestDateComparator

  """
  The change request's ID, such as to exclude change requests that a user
  dismissed.
  """
  id: ChangeRequestIDComparator

  """
  The change request's labels, by name, ignoring case. Currently supports
  GitHub.
  """
  labels: ChangeRequestLabelComparator
}

"""
EXPERIMENTAL: This type may change in a backwards-incompatible way.

TODO(issue: GRAPH-614): 'commit' field should have type GitCommit
before stabilizing this API.
"""
type CodeGraphData implements Node {
  """
  ID of this object that can be used to identify the CodeGraphData
  for pagination in the codeGraphData field.
  """
  id: ID!

  """Coarse description of the data source for this code graph data."""
  provenance: CodeGraphDataProvenance!

  """
  The commit associated with this code graph data.
  
  In general, this will be an ancestor of the commit at which code
  graph data was requested, as code graph data may not be available
  at the exact commit for the blob.
  """
  commit: String!

  """
  Information about the tool which generated this code graph data.
  
  This information may be missing if the tool itself did not specify
  the information in the generated SCIP index. This field is always
  available for all Sourcegraph-maintained indexers.
  """
  toolInfo: CodeGraphToolInfo

  """
  Occurrences are guaranteed to be sorted by range based on
  (start.line, start.character, end.line, end.character) as a 4-tuple.
  It is possible for there to be:
  - Multiple occurrences for the same exact source range.
  - Occurrences which intersect without one containing the other.
  - Occurrences which span across multiple lines.
  
  At the moment, using higher values of 'first:' should not cause
  significantly worst performance.
  
  As an example, for a large C++ codebase, here are the percentiles
  for number of occurrences per document.
  
  | Percentile | Occurrences count |
  |       50   |               241 |
  |       90   |              2443 |
  |       95   |              4554 |
  |       99   |             15869 |
  |       99.9 |             94465 |
  |      100   |            707850 |
  """
  occurrences(first: Int, after: String): SCIPOccurrenceConnection

  """
  Relationships represents additional metadata about how symbols are related
  to each other.
  
  At the moment, this will only return information relationships defined within
  the same file.
  
  E.g. if Dog.java has a class Dog which subclasses Animal defined in
  Animal.java then the IS_IMPLEMENTATION relationship defined on Dog will
  be returned when accessing relationships(..) for Dog.java.
  
  However, this relationship will not show up when accessing relationships(..)
  for Animal.java.
  """
  relationships(first: Int, after: String): SCIPRelationshipConnection
}

"""EXPERIMENTAL: This type may change in a backwards-incompatible way."""
enum CodeGraphDataProvenance {

  Based on a compiler, a type-checker or a similar data source

  """
  SEARCH_BASED
}

"""Mutations on compendia."""
type CompendiaMutation {
  """
  Enqueue a new compendium for a free-text request. Returns immediately with
  state QUEUED; poll the compendium until COMPLETED.
  """
  create(input: CreateCompendiumInput!): Compendium!

  """
  Regenerate a compendium in place. The previous edition is given to the generator
  so the new one keeps its structure where still accurate; chapters whose cited
  code did not change are carried over as they are. With rewrite, every chapter
  is written afresh instead, with the previous edition as a guide to scope only:
  for when the generator itself changed. A no-op while the compendium is already
  generating.
  """
  regenerate(id: ID!, rewrite: Boolean = false): Compendium!

  """
  Regenerate every compendium with an edition that the viewer may see, as
  regenerate does for one, rewrite included: for when the generator itself
  changed. Each is attributed to the viewer and generated as them.
  Compendia already generating are left as they are. Administrators only.
  Returns how many compendia were queued.
  """
  regenerateAll(rewrite: Boolean = false): Int!

  """
  Rewrite some chapters of the current edition against the code at head
  without re-planning the article; the edition number is kept. With no
  chapters given, the chapters the last freshness check found stale are
  revised, along with every chapter that cites code the check saw change.
  A no-op while the compendium is already generating.
  """
  revise(input: ReviseCompendiumInput!): Compendium!

  """
  Ask for an additional diagram of a compendium, e.g. "the request lifecycle".
  Returns immediately with state QUEUED; poll the compendium's requestedDiagrams.
  """
  requestDiagram(input: RequestCompendiumDiagramInput!): CompendiumDiagramRequest!

  """
  Leave a note for the generator: what the next edition should do
  differently. Notes never appear in the compendium; before the next
  regeneration they are distilled into the compendium's standing directions.
  """
  addNote(input: AddCompendiumNoteInput!): Compendium!

  """
  Remove a note. Removing an applied note does not undo its effect on the
  directions.
  """
  deleteNote(id: ID!): Compendium!

  """
  Bind a Deep Search conversation the viewer owns to the part of a
  compendium it was asked about, so it is shown again next to that part.
  Binding the same conversation twice is a no-op.
  """
  attachThread(input: AttachCompendiumThreadInput!): CompendiumThread!

  """Name the compendium's URL: /compendium/{slug}."""
  setSlug(input: SetCompendiumSlugInput!): Compendium!

  """
  Opt the compendium into, or out of, being kept up to date automatically:
  once its edition has drifted from the code it cites and the drift has
  settled, the stale chapters are revised, or a new edition written when
  the code was reorganized, without anyone asking.
  """
  setAutoRefresh(input: SetCompendiumAutoRefreshInput!): Compendium!

  """
  Delete a compendium with every edition, diagram, note and conversation
  binding it has. An edition in the works is abandoned.
  """
  delete(id: ID!): EmptyResponse!
}

  """

  (e.g. per repository, or per-repository-per-language) Has no strict relation
  to the data points shown in the web UI or returned by `points()`, because those
  are aggregated and this number _can_ report some duplicates points which get
  stored but removed at query time for the web UI.
  
  Why its useful: an insight may look like "it is doing nothing" but in reality
  this number will be increasing by e.g. several thousands of points rapidly.
  """
  totalPoints: Int!

  """
  The total number of jobs currently pending to add new data points for this series.
  
  Each job may create multiple data points (e.g. a job may create one data point per
  repo, or language, etc.) This number will go up and down over time until all work
  is completed (discovering work takes almost as long as doing the work.)
  
  Why its useful: signals "amount of work still to be done."
  """
  pendingJobs: Int!

  """
  The total number of jobs completed for this series. Note that since pendingJobs will
  go up/down over time, you CANNOT divide these two numbers to get a percentage as it
  would be nonsense ("it says 90% complete but has been like that for a really long
  time!").

  completedJobs: Int!

  """
  The total number of jobs that were tried multiple times and outright failed. They will
  not be retried again, and indicates the series has incomplete data.

  much data the series data may be missing (e.g. ((30 / 150)*100.0) == 20% of the series

  Why its useful: signals if there are problems, and how severe they are.

  failedJobs: Int!

  effectively be used as a status that the insight is still processing if returned null.

  backfillQueuedAt: DateTime

"""

data from one format into another format. Out-of-band migrations
"""
type OutOfBandMigration implements Node {
  """The unique identifier of this migration."""
  id: ID!

  """The team that owns this migration (e.g., code-intelligence)."""
  team: String!

  """
  The component this migration affects (e.g., codeintel-db.lsif_data_documents).
  """
  component: String!

  """A human-readable summary of the migration."""
  description: String!

  """
  The Sourcegraph version in which this migration was introduced. The format of this version
  includes only major and minor parts separated by a dot. The patch version can always be assumed
  to be zero as we'll never introduce or deprecate an out-of-band migration within a patch release.
  
  It is necessary to completely this migration in reverse (if destructive) before downgrading
  to or past this version. Otherwise, the previous instance version will not be aware of the
  new data format.
  """
  introduced: String!

  """
  The Sourcegraph version by which this migration is assumed to have completed. The format of
  this version mirrors introduced and includes only major and minor parts separated by a dot.
  
  It is necessary to have completed this migration before upgrading to or past this version.
  Otherwise, the next instance version will no longer be aware of the old data format.
  """
  deprecated: String

  """
  The progress of the migration (in the forward direction). In the range [0, 1].
  """
  progress: Float!

  """The time the migration record was inserted."""
  created: DateTime!

  """The last time the migration progress or error list was updated."""
  lastUpdated: DateTime

  """
  If false, the migration moves data destructively, and a previous version of Sourcegraph
  will encounter errors when interfacing with the target data unless the migration is first
  run in reverse prior to a downgrade.
  """
  nonDestructive: Boolean!

  """If true, the migration will run in reverse."""
  applyReverse: Boolean!

  """
  A list of errors that have occurred while performing this migration (in either direction).
  This list is bounded by a maximum size, and older errors will replaced by newer errors as
  the list capacity is reached.
  """
  errors: [OutOfBandMigrationError!]!
}

  """The time the error occurred."""

"""

  """The time the index job stopped running."""

  """The time the upload data file started being processed."""
  processingStartedAt: DateTime

  """The time the upload data file stopped being processed."""
  processingFinishedAt: DateTime

  """The indexing or processing error message."""

  immediately with status QUEUED (content fields null); it never blocks waiting

  content fields are populated. Returns null only when the feature is not
  enabled or the comparison has no base/head commit.

"""
Categorizes a usage based on its relationship to the symbol of interest.

This enum may be expanded in the future.

EXPERIMENTAL: This type may change in a backwards-incompatible way in the future.
"""
enum SymbolUsageKind {
  """
  Denotes a usage as being a definition.
  
  interface Animal:
      sound()
  
  class Dog implements Animal:
      sound() override { ... }
  
  func makeSounds(animal: Animal, dog: Dog):
      animal.sound()
      //     ^---^ (1)
      dog.sound()
      //  ^---^ (2)
  
  Here, usagesForSymbol for (1) will return a Definition usage for Animal.sound().
  Similarly, usagesForSymbol for (2) will return a Definition usage for Dog.sound().
  
  In the general case, a symbol may have multiple definitions.
  Here are some examples:
  
  1. Python allows for multiple inheritance, so the same field can
     be declared in multiple parent classes. In such a situation,
     even Precise results may have multiple definitions.
  2. A function may have different definitions based on the build
     configuration, such as for macOS vs Windows. A precise SCIP indexer
     may unify all such definitions into a single index as SCIP
     currently (as of June 20 2024) doesn't support tracking build
     configuration.
  3. Syntactic or search-based results may not be able to find the
     exact definition, so they may return a superset of the full set
     of definitions.
  """
  DEFINITION

  """
  Denotes a usage as being a reference. References are unified across
  the inheritance hierarchy. For example, consider the following pseudocode:
  
  interface Animal:
      sound()
  
  class Dog implements Animal:
      sound() override { ... }
  
  func makeSounds(animal: Animal, dog: Dog):
      animal.sound()
      //     ^---^ (1)
      dog.sound()
      //  ^---^ (2)
  
  Here, usagesForSymbol for both (1) and (2) will return Reference usages
  for both Animal.sound() and Dog.sound().
  - For (1), it makes sense to also return reference usages for Dog.sound()
    because 'animal' may actually be a Dog.
  - For (2), it makes sense to also return reference usages for Animal.sound()
    because 'dog' value may be up-cast to Animal at some point and the
    and 'sound()' might be called on it after that.
  """
  REFERENCE

  """
  Denotes a usage as being an 'implementation', generally of a method, interface
  or similar (the exact terminology varies across languages - traits, protocols etc.).
  
  For example, consider the following pseudocode:
  
  interface Animal:
  //        ^----^ (1)
      sound()
  //  ^---^ (2)
  
  class Dog implements Animal:
      sound() override { ... }
  
  Here, usagesForSymbol for (1) will return an Implementation usage for Dog.
  Similarly, usagesForSymbol for (2) will return an Implementation usage for Dog.sound().
  
  As of June 20 2024, Implementation usages are only supported by
  Precise indexers. Syntactic and search-based usagesForSymbol will mark all
  such usages as Reference.
  """
  IMPLEMENTATION

  """
  Denotes a usage as being a 'super', generally of a method, type or similar.
  The exact terminology varies across languages and the syntax under question -
  for functions, it might be 'superclass method', 'interface method', 'trait method' etc.
  and for types, it might be 'superclass', 'interface', 'trait' etc.
  
  For example, consider the following pseudocode:
  
  interface Animal:
      sound()
  
  class Dog implements Animal:
      sound() override { ... }
  
  func bark(dog: Dog):
      //         ^-^ (1)
      dog.sound()
      //  ^---^ (2)
  
  Here, usagesForSymbol for (1) will return a Super usage for Animal.
  Similarly, usagesForSymbol for (2) will return a Super usage for Animal.sound().
  
  As of June 20 2024, Super usages are only supported by
  Precise indexers. Syntactic and search-based usagesForSymbol will mark all
  such usages as Reference.
  
  UI note: Strictly speaking, depending on the exact symbol and language under
  consideration, 'Super' usages would be better be grouped under a heading like:
  
  - Method specification (for methods satisfying the signature of an interface
    method in Go or Java)
  - Interface (for types implementing an interface in Go or Java)
  - Trait method (for methods satisfying the signature of a trait method in Rust)
  - Trait (for types implementing a trait in Rust)
  
  and so on. Due to this large variation across languages, we've chosen
  to group all such usages under 'Super' for now.
  
  Historical note: This was previously called 'prototype' in the old API.
  However, 'prototype' has a specific meaning in C++ different from our usage,
  so we recommend avoiding the term 'prototype' in the UI.
  """
  SUPER
}

"""
A place where a symbol is used (defined, referenced, forward-declared, etc.)

EXPERIMENTAL: This type may make backwards-incompatible changes in the future.
"""
type Usage {
  """
  Information about the symbol itself.
  
  This symbol may or may not match the exact input symbol (as specified
  by the source range or directly).
  
  Example: On doing usagesForSymbol for a class Dog which inherits from
  Animal, and is a superclass for Poodle, there may be usages like:
      {
         symbol: { name: "<other stuff> Dog#", ... }
         usageKind: DEFINITION,
         ...
      }
      {
         symbol: { name: "<other stuff>" Dog#", ... }
         usageKind: REFERENCE,
         ...
      }
      {
         symbol: { name: "<other stuff> Animal#", ... }
         usageKind: IMPLEMENTATION,
         ...
      }
      {
         symbol: { name: "<other stuff> Poodle#", ... }
         usageKind: SUPER,
         ...
      }
  
  This information is not provided for search-based usages, because
  they do not have corresponding SCIP symbols which can be used for
  further queries.
  """
  symbol: SymbolInformation

  """Coarse-grained information about the data source."""
  provenance: CodeGraphDataProvenance!

  """
  Opaque fine-grained information describing the data source.
  Provided only for debugging.
  This field should be ignored when checking structural equality.
  """
  dataSource: String

  """Information about where this usage is located."""
  usageRange: UsageRange!

  """The text contents of the line containing the usage."""
  surroundingContent: String!

  """
  Describes the relationship between this usage and the input symbol
  (as specified by the source range or directly).
  """
  usageKind: SymbolUsageKind!
}

"""
EXPERIMENTAL: This type may make backwards-incompatible changes in the future.
"""
type UsageConnection {
  """A single page of Usages."""
  nodes: [Usage!]!

  """Pagination information."""
  pageInfo: PageInfo!
}

"""
EXPERIMENTAL: This type may make backwards-incompatible changes in the future.
"""
type UsageRange {
  """The repository this usage is present in."""
  repository: String!

  """The database ID of the repository this usage is present in."""
  repositoryID: ID!

  """
  TODO(issue: GRAPH-614): 'revision' field should have type GitCommit
  before stabilizing this API.
  """
  revision: String!

  """The root relative path for the file this usage is present in."""
  path: String!

  """
  The source range for the usage.
  
  CAUTION: Depending on the indexer where this data originated from,

  """
  range: Range!
}
